about.title: About
body: Computer Science student at UPPA. Outside of my courses, I learn DevOps and infrastructure engineering by building my own projects, picking up new skills and tools along the way. My goal: to design robust continuous delivery pipelines and industrialize the application lifecycle to make production deployments more reliable.

Passionate about low-level programming and how systems work internally, I aim to understand the mechanisms under the hood rather than follow simple recipes. Most notably, I built my own shell in Python to dive deep into process management, system calls and PATH resolution.
My projects follow a pragmatic philosophy: every infrastructure component addresses a real use case and is configured and provisioned declaratively to guarantee reproducible environments.

items.name: Homelab
items.summary: Infrastructure as Code & Self-Hosting: Deployment of a complete stack on a single-node architecture, provisioned declaratively.
items.stack: Traefik · Prometheus · node-exporter · Grafana · Uptime Kuma · Ansible · Docker Compose · mkcert
bullets: **Traffic Management (Traefik / Reverse Proxy)**: Implementation of a reverse proxy with dynamic service discovery through Docker labels, automatic HTTP-to-HTTPS redirection and TLS certificate lifecycle management (wildcard `*.homelab.lab` via mkcert).

**Observability & Monitoring as Code**: Full industrialization of the monitoring stack (Prometheus, Node Exporter, Grafana, Uptime Kuma): data sources and dashboards are versioned in the repository and hot-provisioned to guarantee complete environment parity.

**Orchestration & Automation (Ansible)**: Design of an idempotent playbook that creates the shared bridge networks and deploys the Docker Compose stacks sequentially, enabling fast Disaster Recovery and fully reproducible infrastructure with a single command.

**Security & Best Practices**: Isolated installation of ansible-core (collections kept in `./.collections`, outside the global `~/.ansible` scope) and strict application of the principle of least privilege (no use of sudo, no modifications to the host system).

items.name: GymTrack
items.summary: A muscle-training tracking application. The goal was never to get an app running, but to build a complete stack and understand it end to end.
items.stack: Python 3.11 · Flask · MySQL 8.0 · Docker Compose · Nginx · Adminer · pytest · GitHub Actions
bullets: **Architecture & Resilience (Docker Compose)**: Multi-container orchestration of a three-tier application. Advanced healthchecks (`condition: service_healthy`) synchronize the Flask API's startup with the MySQL database's actual availability. Data persistence through volumes, network isolation via a dedicated bridge, externalized secrets (`.env`) and automatic bootstrapping of the relational schema.

**Back-end API (Flask)**: Design of a RESTful API with rigorous payload validation, centralized handling of HTTP error codes (400, 409, 500) and joins across up to 4 tables in a 6-table relational schema secured by integrity constraints (FOREIGN KEY and UNIQUE).

**Testing & Code Quality**: Unit and integration test suite built with pytest and unittest.mock, ensuring deterministic behavior with no dependency on a live database (covering nominal cases, edge cases, duplicates and empty payloads).
**CI/CD Pipeline**: GitHub Actions workflow triggered on every push (pytest test validation and container image build). Engineering tasks standardized through a dedicated Makefile.

**Front-end & Delivery**: Front-end served from a lightweight nginx:alpine image (strict separation of concerns, no Python application server involved in serving the front-end), asynchronous fetch calls, native `<dialog>` modals and training metrics visualized with Chart.js.
items.note: *In progress: migration to a cloud deployment on Oracle Cloud Free Tier.*

items.name: Kshell
items.summary: Modular command interpreter: Interactive shell built from scratch in Python.
items.why: to explore and understand a terminal's low-level behavior (launching processes with subprocess, piping between processes, built-ins that change the shell's own state).
bullets: **Execution & Piping**: Execution of binaries found in `$PATH` and command chaining through pipelines (`|`).
**Built-ins**: Implementation of internal commands (cd, pwd, exit, alias, unalias, aide) with built-in user documentation in French.
**Persistence & User Experience (UX)**: Custom aliases saved automatically to `~/.ksh_aliases` and loaded dynamically at each session.
Command and path autocompletion via readline.
Dynamic ANSI-colored prompt showing the current directory and Git branch.
**Architecture**: Rigorously decoupled codebase split into specialized modules (parsing, execution, built-ins, autocompletion, prompt, alias management).
